canonical_question: Does the significant hardness increase after HIP correlate with the precipitation of the 'darker phase' or is it due to other mechanisms like solid solution strengthening?

question_variants.question: Does the significant hardness increase after HIP correlate with the precipitation of the 'darker phase' or is it due to other mechanisms like solid solution strengthening?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes the hardness increase to the HIP process causing the appearance of an HCP phase (dark phase). It notes the distribution of this dark phase differs by casting method (evenly dispersed vs grain boundaries). The text infers that the HCP phase contributes to the hardness increase, but does not explicitly rule out or quantify solid solution strengthening as a competing mechanism in the specific context of the hardness magnitude.

answers.answer: The text states that the HIP process caused the appearance of an HCP phase (observed as a darker phase) and increased hardness. It notes the dark phase distribution differs (evenly dispersed in gravity cast vs concentrated at grain boundaries in suction cast). The text does not explicitly discuss solid solution strengthening in relation to the hardness increase magnitude, but infers the HCP phase is the primary cause of the change.
answers.mechanism: HIP caused appearance of HCP phase (dark phase) and increased hardness.
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit comparison of strengthening mechanisms (precipitation vs solid solution) provided.
evidence_spans: The Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy in the form of buttons was prepared by vacuum arc melting of the nominal mixtures of the corresponding elements.
In order to achieve homogeneous distribution of the elements in the alloys, the buttons were turned upside down and re-melted four times.
One group of specimens was left to solidify inside the mold after casting. Namely, it underwent a process of gravity casting.

source_evidence_spans: It should be noted that the dark phase is evenly dispersed in the matrix of the gravity-assisted casting, while in the case of the suction-assisted casting it is concentrated mostly at the grain boundaries.
